Aisha: Heads up — demo caused a short 503 burst when gw waited on admission. Thinking we need a nonblocking boundary.
Jon: Can you paste the logs? sounds like gateway blocked on lease reconcile.
Aisha: snippet:
2026-03-05T15:02:11Z ingress-gw WARN req=x1 hold=admission wait=920ms
2026-03-05T15:02:11Z admission ERR req=x1 reconcile=slow
2026-03-05T15:02:11Z ingress-gw ERR req=x1 respond=503
Aisha: Proposal idea: AdmitDecision = {OK, PROVISIONAL, DENY} with provisional_ttl and low-prio tag. Gw lets PROVISIONAL in and emits provisional=true metric.
Ravi: That avoids blocking p99 but pushes complexity to reconcile & billing. How do we handle revokes?
Priya: Options: 1) Fast-fail at gw if admission not ready. 2) Provisional token with background reconcile + refunds. Both have fairness effects.
Jon: Proto sketch:
message AdmitDecision { enum State { OK=0; PROVISIONAL=1; DENY=2 } State state=1; string lease=2; int32 ttl_ms=3; }
Ravi: If revoked we need a reconcile pipeline that emits events, refunds, and marks requests as overage if abuse. Idempotency required.
Aisha: Tradeoffs: provisional lowers visible errors, but needs reconciliation metrics (provisional_count, revoked_count, refund_total) and a reliable refund window.
Priya: Suggest experiment: enable provisional only for embeddings/short routes and keep heavy gen on fast-fail. Add short gateway cache (500ms) to reduce stampede.
Jon: Also add simulator for burst patterns to validate fairness and abuse detection before canary.
Ravi: Billing policy: charge on issue, reconcile refunds if revoked. Simpler accounting and discourages abuse.
Aisha: Action items: proto + RFC (Aisha), gateway cache (Jon), reconcile worker + refunds (Ravi), telemetry/dashboard + alerts (Priya). Canary: 1% prod for 48h -> ramp.
Priya: I'll draft metric names and baseline thresholds.
Aisha: Thanks, I'll open the RFC and assign owners.
